Functions build sf_item, sf_scale, sf_choices, sf_branch, sf_check objects exceptions. Rule 2. Every reporting function returns structured object first prints second. object useful downstream code. print method convenience, primary output. Rule 3. text: Items response variables unless type section_break text_block. Required items carry required = TRUE. Item IDs stay stable, response columns reuse analysis plan refers . items measure perceived value (DMPV) tourist satisfaction (TS).
code: intro <- sf_item(   "intro", "About your trip",   type          = "section_break",   section_intro = "Please rate your experience of digital booking and your visit." )  dmpv_1 <- sf_item("dmpv_1", "The destination's online content was trustworthy.",   type = "likert", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5", scale_id = "DMPV") dmpv_2 <- sf_item("dmpv_2", "The online information was consistent across platforms.",   type = "likert", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5", scale_id = "DMPV") dmpv_3 <- sf_item("dmpv_3", "The digital channels offered good value for money.",   type = "likert", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5", scale_id = "DMPV") dmpv_4 <- sf_item("dmpv_4", "I was aware of the destination through digital channels.",   type = "likert", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5", scale_id = "DMPV")  ts_1 <- sf_item("ts_1", "The trip met my expectations.",   type = "likert", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5", scale_id = "TS") ts_2 <- sf_item("ts_2", "My overall travel experience was satisfying.",   type = "likert", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5", scale_id = "TS") ts_3 <- sf_item("ts_3", "I felt comfortable at the destination.",   type = "likert", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5", scale_id = "TS")  visitor_type <- sf_item("visitor_type", "I am a",   type = "single_choice", required = TRUE, choice_set = "visitor")  repeat_change <- sf_item(   "repeat_change", "What changed most since your previous visit?",   type = "textarea", required = FALSE )  attention <- sf_item("attention", "For quality control, please select Agree.",   type = "single_choice", required = TRUE, choice_set = "likert5")

what: CFA syntax: the lower-order measurement model
title: EFA, CFA, CB-SEM, and PLS-SEM syntax generation
text: confirmatory measurement model nine lower-order constructs reflective factors. cfa_lavaan_syntax() writes lavaan syntax model object, need lavaan stage.
code: construct_def <- list(   DMRE = dmre, DMAU = dmau, DMEU = dmeu, DMPV = dmpv,   DSQA = dsqa, DSQT = dsqt, DSUQ = dsuq, TS = ts, BI = bi )  cfa_model <- sf_model(   id    = "lower_order_cfa",   label = "Lower-order measurement model",   type  = "cfa",   constructs = Map(function(id, items) sf_construct(id, id, items),                    names(construct_def), construct_def) )  cat(cfa_lavaan_syntax(model = cfa_model)) #> # lavaan CFA syntax generated by surveyframe #> # Model: Lower-order measurement model #> # Recommended fitting option: std.lv = TRUE #> # Fit with lavaan only when lavaan is installed. #>  #> # DMRE (reflective) #> DMRE =~ dmre_1 + dmre_2 + dmre_3 + dmre_4 #>  #> # DMAU (reflective) #> DMAU =~ dmau_1 + dmau_2 + dmau_3 #>  #> # DMEU (reflective) #> DMEU =~ dmeu_1 + dmeu_2 + dmeu_3 #>  #> # DMPV (reflective) #> DMPV =~ dmpv_1 + dmpv_2 + dmpv_3 + dmpv_4 #>  #> # DSQA (reflective) #> DSQA =~ dsqa_1 + dsqa_2 + dsqa_3 #>  #> # DSQT (reflective) #> DSQT =~ dsqt_1 + dsqt_2 + dsqt_3 + dsqt_4 + dsqt_5 #>  #> # DSUQ (reflective) #> DSUQ =~ dsuq_1 + dsuq_2 + dsuq_3 + dsuq_4 + dsuq_5 #>  #> # TS (reflective) #> TS =~ ts_1 + ts_2 + ts_3 #>  #> # BI (reflective) #> BI =~ bi_1 + bi_2 + bi_3

title: EFA, CFA, CB-SEM, and PLS-SEM syntax generation
text: covariance-based reading treats five constructs first-order reflective factors full item sets, nine direct paths four indirect effects hypotheses. sem_lavaan_syntax() writes measurement, structural, indirect-effect lines.

code: set.seed(2024) n <- 60  # Each construct is driven by a latent score plus item-level noise. # Correlations between constructs are introduced by sharing variance. lat <- function(mu, sigma) pmax(1, pmin(5, round(rnorm(n, mu, sigma)))) add_noise <- function(x, sigma = 0.45) {   pmax(1L, pmin(5L, as.integer(round(x + rnorm(n, 0, sigma))))) }  # Higher service quality and sustainability lift satisfaction. lat_dsqa <- lat(3.7, 0.6) lat_dsqt <- lat(3.6, 0.6) lat_dsuq <- lat(3.5, 0.6) lat_ts   <- pmax(1, pmin(5, round(   0.4 * lat_dsqa + 0.3 * lat_dsqt + 0.2 * lat_dsuq + rnorm(n, 0.6, 0.3) ))) lat_bi   <- pmax(1, pmin(5, round(0.7 * lat_ts + rnorm(n, 0.5, 0.4))))  # Digital marketing constructs are loosely correlated with each other. lat_dmre <- lat(3.8, 0.6) lat_dmau <- pmax(1, pmin(5, round(0.5 * lat_dmre + rnorm(n, 1.9, 0.4)))) lat_dmeu <- pmax(1, pmin(5, round(0.4 * lat_dmre + rnorm(n, 2.2, 0.4)))) lat_dmpv <- pmax(1, pmin(5, round(0.3 * lat_dmre + rnorm(n, 2.5, 0.4))))  # Repeat visitors score slightly higher on satisfaction and intention. visitor_type <- sample(c("first_time", "repeat"), n,                        replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.45, 0.55)) lat_ts[visitor_type == "repeat"] <- pmin(5L, lat_ts[visitor_type == "repeat"] + 1L) lat_bi[visitor_type == "repeat"] <- pmin(5L, lat_bi[visitor_type == "repeat"] + 1L)  # Build item columns from latent scores. make_cols <- function(lat, k, prefix) {   setNames(     as.data.frame(       vapply(seq_len(k), function(i) add_noise(lat), integer(n))     ),     paste0(prefix, seq_len(k))   ) } nationality = sample(       c("thai", "chinese", "japanese", "korean", "indian",         "australian", "british", "german", "american", "other"),       n, TRUE),     education = sample(c("high_school", "diploma", "undergraduate", "post_graduate"),                        n, TRUE, c(0.05, 0.10, 0.48, 0.37)),     profession = sample(c("student", "business", "salaried", "freelancer", "not_working"),                         n, TRUE, c(0.15, 0.20, 0.45, 0.12, 0.08)),     companion = sample(c("friends", "family", "other"),                        n, TRUE, c(0.35, 0.55, text: comments built small phrase bank, seeded example reproducible. north branch’s simulated visits lean positive, south branch’s lean mixed, gives group-role examples something real show, even split leave coincidence. first 4 simulated responses.
code: positive_pool <- c(   "The staff were incredibly friendly and helpful.",   "Check-in was quick and the room was spotless.",   "Our server was attentive and the food arrived fast.",   "The team went out of their way to help us.",   "Friendly staff made the whole visit pleasant.",   "The room was clean and comfortable throughout our stay.",   "Quick service and a warm welcome from everyone.",   "The staff were helpful whenever we needed anything." ) negative_pool <- c(   "We had to wait a long time for someone to help us.",   "The staff seemed rude and unhelpful the whole time.",   "The wait for a table was far too long.",   "Our room was dirty and the service was slow.",   "Staff were slow to respond and not very friendly.",   "The long wait ruined an otherwise average visit.",   "Service was poor and the staff seemed uninterested.",   "We waited a long time and nobody apologised." )  sample_comment <- function(p_positive) {   n_sentences <- sample(1:2, 1)   pools <- sample(c("pos", "neg"), n_sentences, replace = TRUE,                   prob = c(p_positive, 1 - p_positive))   sentences <- vapply(pools, function(p) {     if (p == "pos") sample(positive_pool, 1) else sample(negative_pool, 1)   }, character(1))   paste(sentences, collapse = " ") }  n <- 60 branch <- sample(c("north", "south"), n, replace = TRUE) comments <- vapply(branch, function(b) {   sample_comment(if (b == "north") 0.8 else 0.35) }, character(1))  responses <- data.frame(   satisfaction = sample(3:5, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.2, 0.35, 0.45)),   branch = branch,   comments = comments,   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  kable(head(responses, 4), row.names = FALSE,       caption = "The first 4 simulated responses.")

Install it before fitting. demo   <- sframe_demo_data() scored <- score_scales(demo$responses, demo$instrument) fit    <- lavaan::cfa(syntax, data = scored, std.lv = TRUE) summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE) } # }

title: Render a reproducible survey report — render_report
text: instrument sframe object. data tibble data.frame responses, NULL generate codebook-report. output_file Character NULL. output file path. NULL, temporary file written path returned. output_path Character NULL. Alias output_file. supplied, output_file takes precedence. format Character. Output format: "html" (default) "pdf". PDF output renders HTML report prints pagedown::chrome_print(), requires pagedown package (Suggests) local Chrome Chromium installation. HTML path unchanged. include_quality Logical. Whether include data quality report. Requires data. Defaults TRUE. include_reliability Logical. Whether include reliability diagnostics. Requires data. Defaults TRUE. include_codebook Logical. Whether include instrument codebook. Defaults TRUE. include_missing Logical. Whether include missing-data report. Requires data. Defaults TRUE. include_descriptives Logical. Whether include descriptive statistics. Requires data. Defaults TRUE. include_analysis Logical. Whether include analysis-plan results data supplied instrument analysis_plan. include_models Logical. Whether include saved model JSON generated syntax blocks. Defaults TRUE. plot_palette One "web" (brand colours, -screen reading) "print" (black, grey, white, journal-ready print-friendly report). Applied every chart report embeds. See sframe_brand(). interpretations Named list NULL. Written interpretations keyed analysis-plan block id, added results known. block entry, report section shows pre-declared decision rule "Planned decision rule" label followed written text "Interpretation" label. text: id Character. unique identifier scale. Referenced scale_id argument sf_item(). label Character. human-readable name scale, used reports codebooks. items Character vector. id values items belong scale, listed . Order controls presentation reports, scoring uses item IDs regardless order. Items passed sf_instrument() separate components. method Character. Scoring method. Either "mean" (default) "sum". min_valid Integer NULL. minimum number answered items required compute score respondent, whole number 1 number items. NULL, every item must answered. item whose column absent data counts unanswered. Used score_scales(). reverse_items Character vector NULL. subset items scale reverse-codes. Reversal applies within scale , item can reversed one scale scored answered another. item can also flagged reverse = TRUE sf_item(), reverses within scale named scale_id. reversed item needs declared response bounds, numeric choice set, slider limits rating maximum. weights Numeric vector NULL. Item weights weighted scoring, one positive finite number per item, order items. score_scales() applies weights either method = "mean" method = "sum".

what: Analysis planning, survey statistics, and model syntax
title: surveyframe 0.3.0
text: Added role-based analysis-plan structure preserving old variables/test analysis blocks. New plans can store family, method, roles, options, hypotheses, decision_rule, reporting_references, status, requires_data. Added common survey analysis helpers: descriptives_report(), missing_data_report(), assumption_report(), posthoc_report(), validity_report(), sample_size_plan(). Expanded run_analysis_plan() dispatch v0.3 method registry, including descriptives, missing data, sparse-table tests, related-sample tests, Kendall partial correlations, two-way ANOVA, ANCOVA, repeated ANOVA, ordinal multinomial logistic regression, mediation, moderation, model-syntax output. Added model specification layer: sf_construct(), sf_path(), sf_covariance(), sf_indirect(), sf_model(), validate_model(), model_json(), add_model(), efa_solution(), efa_syntax(), cfa_lavaan_syntax(), sem_lavaan_syntax(), seminr_syntax(), model_report_template(). Syntax generation require lavaan seminr. cfa_syntax() remains available backward-compatible wrapper around cfa_lavaan_syntax(). SurveyBuilder Analyse mode now uses three-panel Plan/Run/Report workspace variable metadata badges, role-based variable assignment, method options, output preview, reporting references, table-based model builder. Significance level shown inferential methods.

title: surveyframe 0.3.0
text: Added export_static_survey(). produces single, self-contained HTML file runs survey modern browser without Shiny server internet connection. thirteen item types fully rendered (Likert, single choice, multiple choice, matrix, numeric, text, long text, date, slider, rating, ranking, section break, text block). Branching logic, required-field validation, progress bar, welcome thank-pages handled client-side JavaScript. submission browser downloads per-respondent CSV file. optional endpoint_url argument adds parallel JSON POST serverless endpoint (Google Apps Script, Netlify function, etc.). exported file suitable hosting GitHub Pages, Netlify, static file server, can also shared directly e-mail attachment opened disk. SHA-256 hash written .sframe files write_sframe() SurveyBuilder HTML computed using canonicalisation algorithm, instruments round-trip correctly browser R.

title: surveyframe 0.3.0
text: Added launch_dashboard(). Opens five-panel Shiny dashboard exploring collected response data alongside instrument definition, without modifying either. panels : Overview (response count, date range, instrument metadata), Items (per-item bar charts, histograms, frequency tables), Scales (scale score distributions mean overlay), Quality (attention-check pass rates), Raw data (scrollable response table CSV download). called without arguments dashboard loads bundled tourism services demo. called user-supplied instrument responses argument, opens metadata-mode showing instrument structure. Added sframe_demo_data(), sframe_input_types_demo_data(), launch_builder_demo(), launch_studio_demo(), launch_dashboard_demo() CRAN-safe examples, training, local GUI testing. Added bundled input-types demo instrument simulated response dataset testing SurveyBuilder, SurveyStudio, dashboard, supported item controls. launch_studio() now accepts preloaded instruments, response data frames, CSV response paths, initial screen selection, host, port, browser control. SurveyStudio reads preloaded values startup.
